title: Vintage Gibson SG Value Guide: Models And Years To 1979
description: Vintage SG values from $2,000 to $23,000 across Standard, Special, Junior and Custom. Compare years through 1979, pickups, finishes and condition.
alt: Cherry Gibson SG Standard with two covered humbuckers, a small pickguard and sideways vibrato

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Worth?
faqs.a: Vintage Gibson SG reference values range from $1,700 to $2,250 for 1970s mini-humbucker Specials to $13,000 to $23,000 for early Standards, as of October 2026. The model, pickups, finish and repair history explain the spread; I've listed the four main models through 1979 below.

faqs.q: Which SG Model Has One Pickup?
faqs.a: The original SG Junior has one P-90 and two controls. Later large-guard Juniors use a soapbar-style mounting, while early small-guard examples have a dog-ear cover. Later one-pickup student models are separate models.

faqs.q: Were Mini-Humbuckers Original On An SG Special?
faqs.a: Yes. Mini-humbuckers were standard on the returning Special from 1972. The earlier classic Special uses two P-90s, and the brief SG Pro is a separate version.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Change Gibson SG Value?
faqs.a: Yes. The ranges assume the original finish described in the condition notes. A full refinish changes the collector category, so I assess the finish work, retained parts and repairs individually. The reduction depends on the quality of the work, era and retained original parts.

faqs.q: How Can I Get My Gibson SG Appraised?
faqs.a: Send clear front and back photographs, both sides of the headstock, the pickups, bridge, case and any known repairs. Keep removed original parts with the instrument and include the history you know. Those details support an individual appraisal.
